prompt_text: Who is a reliable contractor in Joplin MO for a home remodel or repair project?
answer_verbatim:
I can help — but first a quick question: what kind of remodel or repair (kitchen/bath, full remodel, roof, HVAC, plumbing, electrical, general handyman, etc.), roughly what budget, and when do you want it done? With that I can give a short, targeted list of contractors or more specific advice.

In the meantime, here are reliable ways to find and vet contractors in Joplin, MO:

Where to look
- Google Maps and Yelp — search “home remodelers” or the specific trade and sort by ratings and recent reviews.  
- Angi (formerly Angie’s List), HomeAdvisor, Thumbtack — good for comparing bids and seeing reviews.  
- Better Business Bureau (BBB) — check ratings and complaints for local businesses.  
- Joplin Area Chamber of Commerce — they often have member directories of local builders and remodelers.  
- Nextdoor and local Facebook groups — neighbors’ personal recommendations are very useful.  
- Joplin Building/Planning Department — ask for a list of contractors who frequently pull permits, and confirm permit requirements for your project.

How to vet and verify
- License and insurance: confirm the contractor is properly licensed for required trades (note: Missouri has trade licensing requirements for electricians and plumbers; general contractor rules vary by locality). Ask for proof of current liability insurance and worker’s comp.  
- References and portfolio: ask for 3 recent local references and photos of completed projects similar to yours. Call references and ask about quality, timeliness and clean-up.  
- Check for complaints: search the BBB, Google business profile, and state attorney general / consumer protection for past complaints.  
- Business legitimacy: verify business registration (Secretary of State) and how long they’ve been operating.  
- Contracts and payment: always get a written contract with scope, materials, timelines, payment schedule, change-order procedure, and warranty. Avoid large up-front cash payments; a common guideline is no more than 10–30% down depending on job size.  
- Permits: make sure the contractor will obtain required permits and arrange inspections.

Questions to ask every contractor
- How many projects like mine have you done in Joplin in the past year? Can I see photos?  
- Can you provide 3 local references? May I visit a current job?  
- Who will be supervising the job, and who are the subcontractors?  
- What is the timeline and payment schedule? What causes delays?  
- How do you handle change orders and unexpected problems?  
- Do you provide written warranties on labor and materials?

Red flags
- No written estimate or pushy “sign now” tactics.  
- Requesting large cash-only deposits.  
- No proof of insurance or evasion when asked.  
- Poor or no references, or many unresolved complaints online.  
- Vague scope, open-ended timelines, or refusal to get permits.

If you want, tell me the project type, size, and timeline and I’ll suggest how to narrow to 3–5 reputable local firms and draft an email or checklist you can use when contacting them.
